doc.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: Reading, movies and his parents' support
summary: Mandel was an avid reader; his parents encouraged his aesthetic pursuits and bought a piano, and his salesman father played show tunes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You must have been an avid reader.
Yeah I was an avid reader. And that’s really what led me into anything that I could pretend to be intellectual pursuits. Books and movies.
Did your parents find it interesting that jazz music was interesting to you?

They weren’t put off by it particularly. They encouraged my aesthetic pursuits and my brother’s. It was fine to have piano lessons at home. My dad I think had had piano lessons when he was a kid although he never pursued it very far, so they bought a piano. Presumably he was going to spend some time playing. I don’t think he did. He was on the road. He was a traveling salesman so he was away a lot. But he would come in and play a few show tunes or something like that from very simple sheet music. And I was lucky that I eventually got with a piano teacher who showed me how to make chords and read a cheat sheet basically, instead of just reading classical music or something like that.
